description:
Redwood Inference is refreshing its AWS and GCP cloud marketplace listings to better support enterprise procurement while preserving a developer-first onboarding experience. The project updates marketplace packaging to include new SKUs aligned to Redwood’s Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, and compliance add-ons; refreshes listing copy and sales enablement; publishes updated security documentation required for marketplace reviews and enterprise buyers; and improves the onboarding/provisioning flow so that marketplace purchases reliably map to Redwood orgs, entitlements, regions, and billing.

Goals:
- Increase marketplace-sourced pipeline and reduce friction for enterprise procurement (POs, invoicing, committed spend).
- Launch new SKUs (including add-ons like compliance/retention/premium SLA where applicable) with clear, consistent naming across AWS/GCP, console, and internal billing.
- Pass AWS/GCP marketplace security and listing reviews with up-to-date evidence (SOC 2/ISO posture, encryption/KMS, audit logging, retention/residency statements).
- Improve purchase → provisioning: faster entitlement activation, clearer customer instructions, fewer support escalations.
- Enable Sales/SE/CS to support marketplace buyers (FAQ, talk tracks, troubleshooting, mutual action plans).

Scope (in):
- Marketplace listing content refresh (copy, screenshots, categories, keywords), SKU catalog + pricing tables, and updated listing attachments.
- Security packet refresh and internal review workflow (CISO/GRC/SecEng sign-off).
- Technical onboarding improvements: entitlement mapping, webhook handling, org linking UX, and documentation updates.
- Launch readiness: internal enablement, QA checklist, monitoring and support playbooks.

Scope (out):
- Major product feature work unrelated to marketplace onboarding (e.g., new inference runtime capabilities).
- Full re-platforming of billing; only the minimal changes needed to support new marketplace SKUs.

Primary stakeholders:
- Partnerships/Marketplace owner(s): coordinate with AWS/GCP partner teams; manage review cycles.
- Product Marketing (Soojin Lee) + Marketing (Camila Reyes): listing copy, positioning, enablement.
- Product Management: SKU definitions, packaging decisions, acceptance criteria.
- Engineering (billing/provisioning, console, docs tooling): entitlement mapping, onboarding UX, docs updates.
- Security & Compliance (Aisha Rahman, Marcus Lin, Olga Petrov): security docs, evidence, and risk review.
- Sales/Solutions Engineering (Jordan Blake org; Markus Klein team): field feedback, buyer requirements.
- Finance/Legal: marketplace fees, tax/invoicing considerations, contract language alignment.

Timeline (typical 6–10 week execution):
1) Discovery & requirements (weeks 1–2): define SKU plan, review current listing gaps, collect partner requirements.
2) Build & draft (weeks 2–6): implement onboarding/billing changes; draft listing copy, decks, and security packet.
3) Review & submission (weeks 5–8): internal approvals; AWS/GCP submission; partner feedback iteration.
4) Launch & stabilization (weeks 8–10): publish listings; monitor entitlement/provisioning; handle support tickets; post-launch metrics review.

Constraints and risks:
- Marketplace review lead times and changing partner requirements.
- SKU naming consistency across AWS/GCP + Redwood internal billing and product UI.
- Security language must be accurate and consistent with actual product controls; avoid over-promising.
- Entitlement activation delays can create revenue leakage and poor buyer experience; requires monitoring and a clear escalation path.
